notes: GR4 obliges ENABLE I-O TERMINAL to activate the path from the SYMBOLIC TERMINAL source to the program, with the Table 1 statuses; every probe shows that (00 on a disabled terminal, 15 again, 40, 21, a SEND held until ENABLE and delivered after). The refuter's question is whether a RECEIVE before ENABLE (or after DISABLE) must find no message the MCS already holds for the terminal. The text does not require it: GR1 says the ENABLE 'is not required' when the connection 'is to be handled by some other means external to this program' and that 'the logical path ... between the COBOL programs and the MCS is not affected by the ENABLE statement', so the part of the source-to-program path that ENABLE controls is the source's link INTO the MCS; and RECEIVE GR5 makes 'the conditions under which data is not made available' implementor-defined. Whether a message the MCS holds at start for a terminal configured disabled has crossed that link is therefore the implementor's MCS. Precedence: GnuCOBOL 3.2 implements no MCS (set4 probe g1), IBM Enterprise COBOL has no communication module, Micro Focus not checked; the recorded design (DESIGN-communication-facility.md 'Logical paths': the flag closes the terminal's link to the MCS, TakeFromTerminal asks nothing of it) is the choice, and it is applied consistently (m1: held BYE and HI delivered with or without ENABLE; m2: after DISABLE I-O TERMINAL a held message is still received, and a SEND is 10). Implementor choice: Does a RECEIVE through an I-O CD find a message the MCS already holds for its terminal while the terminal's path is not active? Decided by the implementor (§1985:XIV.3.5.4 GR5; §1985:XIV.3.3.4 GR1); GnuCOBOL 3.2 and IBM Enterprise COBOL implement no MCS, so WiseOwl's recorded design choice stands; documented in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.3, row "ENABLE and DISABLE I-O TERMINAL and a message the MCS holds".
